w:r.w:t: Bias-Resilient Meeting Onboarding – Advanced 6-Minute Assessment
Purpose: Sharpen personalization for users who completed the core profile. Tone: plain language, non-clinical. No diagnostic intent.
Instructions: Answer quickly and honestly. Completion time about 6 minutes.
1) Framing Micro-game
A rollout has a 90 percent chance of success and a 10 percent chance of failure.
Which message would you send to the team?
1) Emphasize the 90 percent success chance. 2) Emphasize the 10 percent risk and mitigation.
Confidence 0 to 100 percent: __
2) Emotion Regulation Style
Rate 1 to 5.
1. When upset, I reframe the situation to see it differently. (reappraisal)
2. I hold back my emotions so others do not notice. (suppression)
3. I look for the lesson in difficult events. (reappraisal)
4. I keep a neutral face even when I feel strong emotion. (suppression)
5. I try to view challenges as temporary. (reappraisal)
6. I bottle things up during meetings. (suppression)
3) Relationship Comfort and Independence
Rate 1 to 5.
1. I appreciate honest feedback even when it stings.
2. I worry that teammates will think poorly of me if I disagree. (anxious)
3. I am comfortable asking for help when I need it.
4. I downplay my needs to avoid bothering others. (avoidant)
5. I can be direct without fearing rejection.
6. I pull back when others want to discuss feelings. (avoidant)
7. I seek reassurance during tense discussions. (anxious)
8. I can disagree and still feel connected to the team.
4) Listening Style
Choose the option that fits you best.
1. When listening I focus mostly on: a) the person, b) the content, c) the time.
2. My default note style is: a) paraphrases, b) facts and numbers, c) action items.
3. When discussion speeds up I tend to: a) ask for examples, b) summarize, c) push for decisions.
4. Under pressure I: a) get quiet, b) double check details, c) become brief and direct.
5. I want nudges that help me: a) empathize, b) clarify logic, c) be concise.
6. I prefer meeting pace: a) slower with reflection, b) balanced, c) fast with decisions.
5) Perspective Taking and Thin-Slice Rating
A. Read the sentence: “I think we should try a different approach next quarter.”
What are two possible positive intentions behind this statement? 1) __ 2) __
B. In the app a 10 second clip will play. Rate the speaker’s affect. Warmth 1 to 5: __ Energy 1 to 5: __ Confidence 1 to 5: __
6) Loss Aversion Choice Pair
Choose one:
A) A sure gain of 400 dollars.
B) A 50 percent chance to gain 900 dollars and a 50 percent chance to gain 0 dollars.
Now choose one:
C) A sure loss of 400 dollars.
D) A 50 percent chance to lose 900 dollars and a 50 percent chance to lose 0 dollars.
7) Intent Attribution Vignette 2 (optional)
You present a plan and receive a short “Let’s discuss” message with no details. What is your first interpretation?
Choose one: a) They want to collaborate. b) They are unhappy with the plan. c) They need clarification. d) They want to delay the decision.
Confidence 0 to 100 percent: __
8) Data Quality Item
Attention check: Please select option 3 here. 1 2 3 4 5
Engineering Scoring and Nudge Rules
• Framing: If user selects success frame consistently with confidence ≥ 70, raise prompts to include risk and mitigation. If selects risk frame, suggest balancing with upside.

• Emotion regulation: Compute reappraisal mean (items 1,3,5) and suppression mean (items 2,4,6). If suppression ≥ reappraisal + 0.5, enable feel-then-fact scripts and breathing pause prompts. If reappraisal > suppression by 0.5, prefer succinct reframes.

• Relationship comfort: Compute anxious mean (items 2,7) and avoidant mean (items 4,6). If anxious ≥ 3.8, increase reassurance and acknowledgment prompts; if avoidant ≥ 3.8, reduce emotional probes and favor clarity and facts.
• Listening style: Map a/b/c choices to coaching tone. a → empathy framing; b → logic and structure; c → brevity and action. Use the dominant choice across six items.
• Perspective taking: If user lists two positive intentions, reduce empathy prompts; if blank or one, add paraphrase-then-propose nudges. Thin-slice ratings can calibrate tone sensitivity.
• Loss aversion: If A and D are chosen (reflection pattern), enable evaluate both upside and downside evenly prompts.
• Intent vignette 2: Hostile or delay interpretations with confidence ≥ 70 activate benefit-of-the-doubt prompts and request one specific example.
• Validity: If attention check fails, flag low data quality for this session.
